title: Leadership team effectiveness checklist (free, Word)
description: A free leadership team effectiveness checklist: 20 statements on set-up, meetings, team states and outcomes, for each member to answer alone, then compare.
lead: Twenty statements a leadership team answers about itself, one layer at a time. They cover how it is set up, how it works, what has built up between members and what it delivers. Each member answers alone, then the team compares. It is a Word file you can change as you like.
teaser: Twenty statements across the four layers in this article, each with the research it comes from. Each member answers alone, and the team talks about where answers differ.

items: **Conditions.** Six statements on membership, purpose, shared tasks, size, skills and support.
**Processes.** Seven statements on meetings: a goal for each item, focus, speaking up, problem solving, disagreement, the whole organisation first and review.
**States.** Three statements on safety, trust and acting as one team.
**Outcomes.** Four statements on direction, commitment, the team's ability to keep working together and members' growth.
**Next steps.** Room to record where answers differ, the layer you will work on first and the date of the next check.

blocks.text: Give the checklist to every member before a meeting. Each answers Yes, Partly or No to every statement, alone. Answers given alone show where views differ; a discussion that starts with one view tends to hide it.
In the meeting, start with the statements where answers differ most. Pick one layer to work on, starting with the conditions if they are weak. Check again in a few months.

blocks.title: A checklist, not a score
blocks.text: It has no score, no cut-offs and no benchmark. It is a way to start a conversation, not a tested measure. If people hold back when answers are compared openly, collect them anonymously first.
Why is it built this way?

The statements follow the four layers in [leadership team effectiveness](/articles/what-makes-a-leadership-team-effective): conditions, processes, states and outcomes. Each statement names the research it comes from, and the article lists every source in full. Methods and survey questions are in [how to assess a leadership team](/articles/how-to-assess-a-leadership-team).
